caption: The 2027 Bells Beach Surf Film Festival is just over four months away. Our festival committee have been working hard behind the scenes planning to bring you the best surf films from Australia and around the world. We have some big surprises planned for 2027... film submissions still welcome - email; bellsbeachsff@gmail.com ! 🌊🎬🍿

Tonight is Opening Night of the 2026 Bells Beach Surf Film Festival in Torquay. The festival is held at the Australian National Surfing Museum, 77 Beach Road, Torquay. We have also decided not to have beers this year... other liquid refreshments will be provided. Doors open at 7.30pm. Films start at 8.00pm!

It is awards time and after much deliberation our festival committee chose to give SURFING WITH A PENGUIN the Best Short Film Award. The film screened to a highly appreciative audience who laughed and sighed with wonder at the way the penguin interacted with you and other surfers in South Africa. We all loved the way the telling was overlain with the ecological message of how we all need to value, respect and protect our ecosystems. A deserving winner!

Well that is a wrap for another year. We are still buzzing from Closing Night which featured a full house, filmmakers in the house (and a fascinating pre-recorded interview with Tim Bonython who was in Nazare), two World Premiere's and four amazing surf films including SWELL CHASING - MULLAGHMORE which was filmed two weeks ago and featured 30 foot plus bombs in huge cold Irish waves. Great vibes all night. A huge that's to our amazing festival committee - Katey, Ted, Glen, Bruce and John who work hard all year finding films and then presenting them in Torquay. Thanks also to Craig Baird and Pete Murphy at the Australian National Surfing Museum who looked after us each night. Thanks to our dedicated audiences who turn up each year and a massive shout out to the surf filmmakers around the world who create the surf films we get to enjoy on the big screen. 2026 was huge... a hard act to follow but we will be back with another surf films festival in January 2027! (photos courtesy Katey Shearer Photography)

We are stoked to announce that Andrew Kaineder's film INNER MECHANICS has won BEST CINEMATOGRAPHY at this years surf film festival. Our festival committee recognised the beautiful photography and amazing angles through which Andrew and Russell told us about the thinking behind Russell Bierke's approach to those amazing waves. We know the festival has now given INNER MECHANICS the same award for cinematography that Kaineder and his team won last year for "The Outer Edge of Leisure" but we have to say both are outstanding examples of the craft of surf filmmaking. The committee especially loves the wonderful way Kaineder weaved the images of Russell's surfing into the interviews revealing how he is able to prepare and drop into those beautiful but intimidating slabs. 

We highly recommend that you check this film out on a big screen. It is awesome!

The 16th Bells Beach Surf Film Festival will run from Saturday 2nd - Tuesday 5th January 2027. Three nights of amazing surf films from Australia and overseas PLUS a super special event night on Tuesday 5th!!!! The Festival Committee are currently finalising the programme. Tickets on sale first week of December. Stay tuned!📽️ 🎸 🏄‍♀️

We are still buzzing after a huge Opening Night at the festival last night. Great films, great crowd, great vibe... and we had cake for everyone to celebrate our 15th anniversary! No cake tonight but five amazing surf films with filmmakers in attendance. Another night of action on the big screen at the 2026 Bells Beach Surf Film Festival!

Tonight is Closing Night of the 2026 Bells Beach Surf Film Festival. We are very excited tonight to have the World Premiere of Katey Shearer's latest surf film HOME. Filmed on the Surf Coast and combining Super 8mm footage with digital video HOME is a beautiful film exploring themes of country and coast. The festival will close with a BIG mystery film which we believe is also a theatrical World Premiere.... we can't tell to what it is but it is mind-blowing!!!! Another night of great surf films on the big screen... only at the Bells Beach Surf Film Festival.

For @alexandermegos , Siurana is more than just a climbing destination. It’s a place where he has grown as a climber, returning throughout his career to take on some of its most iconic and demanding routes. Over the years, his story has become part of the area’s climbing history and community. 
In 2013, Alex made history on Estado Crítico (9a), completing the world’s first 9a onsight. Just days later, he climbed La Rambla (9a+), one of Siurana’s most celebrated routes, first ascended by Ramón Julián Puigblanque, on his second attempt.
Over the years, Alex continued returning to Siurana. In 2021, he completed three of the La Capella sector’s hardest routes: King Capella, La Furia de Jabalí, and La Capella. In 2024, Alex made the first repeat of Chris Sharma’s Sleeping Lion (9b), a route later climbed by fellow Tenaya athlete Sachi Amma.
Through years of visits, hard climbs, and memorable ascents, Alex has become part of Siurana’s history. This year, we’re excited to welcome him to the @siuranaclimbingfestival 

📷 @esteban.ele.eme (1,2,3,7), Miguel Catita (4), @marcozanone (5), @christoph_hanke (6)

📣 IMPORTANT ANNOUNCEMENT📣
The Nightcliff Arts, Music & Culture Committee are saddened to announce that the Nightcliff Seabreeze Festival will be a biennial festival. This means we will have a break in 2027, and come back in 2028 with a bang! 

This has not been an easy decision for us, however with the rising pressure, increasing costs, decreasing funding and the amount of work involved for a small committee - we have decided that we need more time for planning and ensuring that we deliver the best festival possible. 

If you have any queries, or concerns please contact namcisecretary@gmail.com

We will continue to work on improving the Festival throughout 2027, if you are interested in joining the committee or becoming involved, please contact namcisecretary@gmail.com

We mourn the passing of one of Sheffield’s great mural artists, John Eathorne of West Tamar, Tasmania.

John left a lasting mark on our town, painting many beautiful murals and achieving recognition as a multi International Mural Fest Finalist. 

Across a career spanning more than four decades, John worked as a freelance commercial artist specialising in sign writing, murals, and fine art portraiture with projects commissioned throughout Australia and internationally. 

You will be greatly missed John, but your work and your legacy will remain part of Sheffield and the Kentish Municipality forever. ❤️

BETWEEN Spread and Gathering
A Relay Project Across Asian Art Book Fairs

本企画は、現在進行形で育まれているアジアの出版実践の記録を目的に、アジア各地のアートブックフェアを巡回するリレープロジェクトです。選者はアジアのブックデザインを切り口に20冊の本を選び、次の土地へ手渡していきます。選書は「ベスト・オブ」を決めるためのものではなく、その時点での選者の本棚や関心を反映した個人的な視点から行います。

前の土地から受け取った本は、現地のデザイナーが選書を読み解き、ポスターへと翻訳し、現地チームによる新たな選書とともにブックフェアの開催時期にあわせて展示され、さらに次の土地へと旅を続けます。約1年間の巡回を通して、本、言葉、グラフィック、人々の対話が重なり、2027年刊行予定の記録集へと結実していきます。

アートブックフェアは、本プロジェクトの会場であると同時に、その方法（Method）でもあります。単なる展示や販売の場ではなく、本づくりをともに行うための場と捉え、出会い、対話し、翻訳し、手渡していくプロセスそのものを共有し、ともに育てていくことを目指しています。

Episode 1 Singapore

BETWEENの最初の巡回地はシンガポールです 🇸🇬

本日8月30日には、Singapore Art Book Fair（inSGABF）のラジオプログラム「Radio Radio Radio」にて、BETWEENのプロジェクトと、日本・シンガポールで行われた選書についてお話しします。

そしてSGABF翌日の8月31日からは、移転後オープンしたばかりのTemporary Unitにて展覧会を開催します。

会場では、日本とシンガポールでそれぞれ選ばれた20冊、計40冊のアートブックと、シンガポールを拠点に活動するgideon-jamieが日本チームの選書を読み解き、ポスターへと翻訳した作品を展示します。

日本からシンガポールへ本が手渡され、そこで新しい本とグラフィックが加わり、次の土地へと旅を続けていきます。

本をきっかけに、さまざまな出会いや開かれた対話が生まれる機会となれば嬉しいです。

最後にSGABF直前にも関わらず協力してくれたシンガポールの友人たちに心から感謝します。ありがとう。

New exhibition!

@between__spread_and_gathering is a relay project travelling across art book fairs in Asia, documenting publishing practices as they continue to evolve across the region. Through the lens of book design, selectors in each location would choose twenty books from their bookshelves and pass them on to the next location. The selection is not intended to represent each place or define a “best of,” but rather reflects the selectors’ personal perspectives — the books on their shelves and their interests at that particular moment.Books received from the previous location are interpreted by local designers and translated into posters, then exhibited alongside a new selection made by the local team before continuing their journey to the next location. Over the course of this year-long relay, books, words, graphics, and conversations accumulate and intersect, with the process ultimately documented in a publication scheduled for 2027.The first stop of the relay is Singapore. The exhibition at 
Temporary Unit brings together forty art books — twenty selected in Japan and twenty in Singapore — alongside a poster created by gideon-jamie in response to the Japanese selection. We hope the books will become starting points for new encounters and open conversations.This project is organised and initiated by Naoko Higashi (@tokyoartbookfair), Daisuke Kano, Toshiaki Koga, and Yuma Wada, with Atelier HOKO, Catherine Hu, gideon-jamie, and Renée Ting (@singaporeartbookfair) joining for the first stop in Singapore.

昨年のTOKIO ART BOOK FAIR、SKAC (SKWAT KAMEARI ART CENTRE) に続き、5月29日（金）〜31日（日）の3日間、福岡・太宰府天満宮にて行われる
Pages | Fukuoka Art Book Fairでも「BOOK?」をご紹介します。
また、5月29日（金）にはAtelier HOKOによるトークイベントも予定しています。
お近くの方は、ぜひお越しください！

-—
TOKYO ART BOOK FAIR is presenting the Japan touring exhibition “BOOK?” by Atelier HOKO.
Following presentations at TOKIO ART BOOK FAIR and SKWAT / twelvebooks last year,
“BOOK?” will next be featured at Pages | Fukuoka Art Book Fair, taking place from May 29 (Fri) to 31 (Sun) at Dazaifu Tenmangu in Fukuoka.
A talk event by Atelier HOKO is also scheduled for May 29 (Fri).
If you are nearby, we would love to see you there!

—

BOOK?
Atelier HOKO（アトリエ・ホコ）は、2002年に設立されたインディペンデントのリサーチユニットで、現在はシンガポールを拠点に活動しています。本展では、デジタルメディアが広がり、私たちと物理的な世界との関わり方が変化しつつある今、本を読む行為にまつわる人間のふるまいや感覚について、さまざまな「問い」を来場者に投げかけます。本のサイズや形状、紙の質感は、読書体験にどのような影響を与えているのでしょうか。見慣れたソフトカバーの雑誌が、もし豪華なハードカバーだったら？ あるいは、本がページを閉じることを拒んだとしたら？ 素朴な疑問や想像から着想を得た多様なアプローチを通して、本展は「本」という存在をあらためて多角的に見つめ直す機会をひらきます。それは懐古主義ではなく、私たちが「読む」という行為の本質へ立ち返るための試みです。

Talk: So… What is a Book?
5月29日（金）13:00-14:00 @ 太宰府天満宮文書館
登壇者：Alvin Ho 、Clara Koh（Atelier HOKO）

—

Atelier HOKO
Atelier HOKOは、Alvin Ho と Clara Koh によって設立され、日常のありふれた物や身近な現象を探究するリサーチユニットとして活動しています。彼らが発行する定期刊行物『Science of the Secondary（取るに足らない科学）』では、りんご、窓、トイレットペーパー、ストローなど毎号ひとつのテーマを掲げ、ありふれた物事をフラットかつオープンな視点で実践したリサーチ結果をまとめています。

kyotoartbookfair.com

2006年にNY Art Book Fairが始まって以降、アートブックフェアは世界各地へと広がり、本を媒介に作り手と読者が出会う文化的な場として育まれてきました。
京都には、長い時間をかけて受け継がれてきた文化や技術があり、出版や表現に関わるさまざまな人や場所が、それぞれの活動を続けながら独自の文化を育んできました。KABFでは、そうした京都固有の環境とアートブックフェアという場を交差させることで、ここでしか生まれない出会いや交流のあり方を探っていきます。
回を重ねるごとに、京都という土地の時間や人々の関係性の中からKABFらしさを形成し、この場所でしか成立しないブックフェアを目指します。

主催：京都アートブックフェア実行委員会

---

In May 2027, a new art book fair, the KYOTO ART BOOK FAIR (KABF), will take place in Kyoto.
The TABF office has also joined the executive committee, and preparations for the first edition are now underway.
The call for exhibitors is scheduled to open in late October 2026.

Dates: Friday, May 21 – Sunday, May 23, 2027
Venue: Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art
kyotoartbookfair.com

Since the NY Art Book Fair began in 2006, art book fairs have spread to cities around the world, growing into cultural spaces where makers and readers meet through books.
Kyoto is home to culture and craft passed down over a long span of time, and to diverse people and places involved in publishing and creative expression, each continuing its own work while nurturing a culture of its own. KABF will bring this environment, particular to Kyoto, together with the art book fair, exploring forms of encounter and exchange that can only emerge here.
With each edition, KABF aims to shape a character of its own from the time accumulated in Kyoto and the relationships among its people, and to become a book fair that could only exist in this place.

Organized by: KYOTO ART BOOK FAIR Executive Committee

News from “TABF 2025 Talent Award”

April 24 – May 31 Unbidden Tongues @ NEW COVER

Congratulations once again to @unbidden_tongues  Thank you for your generous support, @neutral_colors_magazine @new_cover_bookshop 

TABF2025では、新たな才能の発掘と支援を目的に掲げ、全出展者を対象とするアワード「𝙏𝘼𝘽𝙁 𝙏𝙖𝙡𝙚𝙣𝙩 𝘼𝙬𝙖𝙧𝙙」を開催しました。6組の選者が「最も推したい出展者」を1組選出し、それぞれの受賞者には、アーティスト長谷川有里によるTABF特製トロフィーと、選者からの副賞が贈られました。

WEEK 2の選者、NEUTRAL COLORSの加藤直徳さん、加納大輔さんは会場をじっくり見て、オランダの出版社Unbidden Tonguesを選出しました。

「これらは歴史的記念碑でもなければコレクターズアイテムでもない。報告書や婦人科の記録、忘れ去られた視覚詩など、これまで注目されることのなかった言葉の数々を、彼らは拾い上げる。1色のみで印刷された安価な出版物は、広く届けることを可能にし、「招かれざる舌」はあらゆる場所に忍び込む。薄くささやかな冊子に空けられた二つの穴が、この先に重なる厚みを予感させる」加納大輔

「一見すると地味な白い紙が並ぶブース構成に違和感を感じた。穴の位置もおかしい。またか、、、難解なコンセプトを提示されるのかと身構えてしまったからだ。しかしだんだんと意味がわかってくるにつれて、薄い紙たちが束ねられアートブックが現出する。しかもシンプルかつ明快なアートブックとして。これが並んでいることこそが可能性だ。たとえ資金が潤沢でなかったとしても、世界に声を行き渡らせることができる」加藤直徳

そして副賞として、NEUTRAL COLORSの書店NEW COVERでのフィーチャーが決定し、現在Unbidden Tanguesのメインプロジェクトである10冊をご覧いただけます。

TABFの雑踏の中でも、静かに、しかし確かな強さをもって響いていたUnbidden Tongues。
NEW COVERでは、その声が丁寧にすくい上げられ、紹介されています。

TABFでゆっくり見られなかった方、興味を持たれた方、ぜひこの機会にじっくりとご覧ください！

TOKYO ART BOOK FAIR(TABF) are pleased to announce that will participate in Under The Leaf - Book Fair, a two-day festival held in Helsinki, Finland.

During the fair, TABF will present 𝚄𝚗𝚍𝚎𝚛 𝚃𝚑𝚎 𝙻𝚒𝚗𝚎𝚜 an exhibition focusing on illustration and drawing. The exhibition will feature around 30 titles of art book and zines by artists based in Japan, published in recent years.

Hikari Nishida @hikanishida , artist and co-organizer of Under The Leaf – Book Fair, previously served as a curator for the Nordic Art Book Store as part of TABF 2023’s special program Guest Country vol.7: Nordic Countries. BETWEEN Spread and Gathering — Singapore

Today is the final day of the first stop of our relay in Singapore. A little belatedly, we’d like to share some scenes from the exhibition at Temporary Unit.

The exhibition brings together 40 books—20 selected in Japan and 20 in Singapore—alongside posters by Singapore-based gideon-jamie, who interpreted the Japanese selection and translated it into a new graphic form.

Throughout the exhibition, many people have spent time with the books, talked around them, and shared their thoughts. We hope to carry these encounters and conversations with us as part of the ongoing record of the project.

The books passed from Japan to Singapore have been joined by new books, words, graphics, and encounters here, and BETWEEN will now continue its journey to the next location.

A huge thank you to Gideon & Jamie, Atelier HOKO, Renée Ting, and Catherine Hu for making this project possible in Singapore, as well as to all the publishers and artists who contributed their books, and everyone who came to visit the exhibition. Thank you for being part of the first stop of BETWEEN!

Today, 19 September, is the final day. Posters by gideon-jamie are also available for purchase at Temporary Unit. If you’re in Singapore, please stop by!

SINGAPORE ART BOOK FAIR 2026: smaller edition

TOKYO ART BOOK FAIR（TABF）は、シンガポールで開催されるSingapore Art Book Fair（SGABF）に参加します。

TABFのブースでは、TABFが制作した出版物に加え、TABFゆかりの出展者の皆さんによる本をご紹介します。

Thing Booksが主催するSGABFには、初回を含めこれまで3回参加してきました。毎回、素晴らしい出展者の方々やアートブック、ZINEとの出会いがあり、ウェルカムな雰囲気も心地よく、さまざまなチャレンジからいつもたくさんの刺激をもらっています。

今年はAtelier HOKOをアートディレクターとして迎え、初の「smaller edition」を開催。どのようなアートブックフェア体験になるのか、今から期待しています。毎日“席替え”もあるそうなので、いろいろな出展者の方たちと交流できるのも嬉しいところです。

シンガポールにいらっしゃる方は、ぜひこの実験的なフェアを目撃しに遊びにいらしてください！皆さんとお会いできることを楽しみにしています。

また、8月31日からはTemporary Unitにて、TABFの新しいリレープロジェクト「BETWEEN Spread and Gathering」の展示も開催します。アジア各地のアートブックフェアを巡りながら、本、デザイン、人をつないでいくプロジェクトです。こちらもあわせて、ぜひお越しいただけると嬉しいです！

TOKYO ART BOOK FAIR (TABF) is heading to Singapore Art Book Fair (SGABF)!

At our booth, we’ll present TABF publications alongside a selection of books by publishers and artists connected to TABF.

This will be our fourth time participating in SGABF since its first edition. We’ve always loved its welcoming atmosphere, the encounters with inspiring exhibitors, art books and zines, and the new challenges the fair takes on each year.

This year, SGABF is experimenting with its first “smaller edition.” We’re excited to see what kind of art book fair experience will emerge. We also hear that exhibitors will change tables every day, so we’re happy to have the chance to meet and connect with many different exhibitors!

If you’re in Singapore, come experience this experimental edition with us. We look forward to seeing you there!

From 31 August, we’ll also present BETWEEN Spread and Gathering at Temporary Unit—a new TABF relay project connecting books, design and people across art book fairs in Asia. We hope you’ll come by!

Some films start with a clear plan… and some grow naturally from the moments along the way. Moments in Passing is one of those special ones.
Four mates packed into an old Toyota Hiace, chasing waves around Aotearoa and capturing the journey on Super 8 and 16mm film.
Months later, while visiting his grandfather in Westport as his health began to decline, the filmmaker @dano.fletcher started recording an audio diary of his grandfather’s life. That moment became the thread that tied the whole project together — blending surf travel, friendship, and whānau into something truly personal.
A beautiful, reflective piece about memory, connection, gratitude and the moments that shape us.

Selected by Naonori Kato & Daisuke Kano (NEUTRAL COLORS)

選評：
「一見すると地味な白い紙が並ぶブース構成に違和感を感じた。…（中略）しかしだんだんと意味がわかってくるにつれて、薄い紙たちが束ねられアートブックが現出する。しかもシンプルかつ明快なアートブックとして。これが並んでいることこそが可能性だ。たとえ資金が潤沢でなかったとしても、世界に声を行き渡らせることができる」（加藤直徳）

「これらは歴史的記念碑でもなければコレクターズアイテムでもない。報告書や婦人科の記録、忘れ去られた視覚詩など、これまで注目されることのなかった言葉の数々を、彼らは拾い上げる。…」（加納大輔）

📖 王格勒 𝗚𝗲𝗹𝗲 𝗪𝗮𝗻𝗴 
Selected by Roger Willems (Director, Roma Publications)
｜Prize: Sigma BF ※2

選評：
I was especially struck by the book he created about the supermarket owned by his mother. His drawings (with text notes) depict mini events and daily routines noted while working there himself. Another project is about disappearing local community structures in Chinese building areas. The publications are handmade, printed in small editions, which he sells for very little. Amazing.

📖 𝗣𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗶𝘁 𝗕𝗹𝗮𝗰𝗸
Selected by Renée Ting (Director, Singapore Art Book Fair)
｜Prize: Complimentary booth at the next Singapore Art Book Fair ※3

選評：
Taking that into consideration, the way they work with artists of various mediums to translate their practices into the art book format shows a lot of respect and sensitivity to the medium.
For example, for one of their books, they chose to only include one line as a description or colophon, and that feels like a non-intrusive way of presenting a video artist’s work that has to do with camera surveillance (a seemingly intrusive act).

※2　Additional prize provided by @sigma_japan
※3　Recipients are responsible for their own travel, accommodation, and all other expenses related to participation.

Entre máquinas inestables, dibujos microscópicos y personajes que rozan lo absurdo, Ricardo Lanzarini reconstruye aquí el hilo vital de su obra. La entrevista recorre los núcleos conceptuales de su exposición y libro "Electrocardiograma escultórico", y se abre a un relato donde la ironía y la experimentación, la escucha atenta de los espacios y un imaginario tan íntimo como indócil sostienen una práctica en permanente transformación.

Amid unstable machines, microscopic drawings, and characters that verge on the absurd, Ricardo Lanzarini traces the vital thread of his practice. The interview follows the conceptual cores of his exhibition and book “Sculptural Electrocardiogram”, opening onto a narrative where irony and experimentation, an attentive listening to space, and an imagination as intimate as it is unruly sustain a practice in constant transformation.

Few people have been part of ASFF from the very beginning, and Craig — better known as @photocpl — is one of them. A founding ASFF judge, Craig is an internationally award-winning photographer and widely regarded as one of Aotearoa’s most respected surf photographers.
Beyond the lens, Craig has worn many hats. He’s the former Editor-in-Chief of New Zealand Surfing Magazine and the force behind Photo CPL Media, publishing 11 hardcover photography books. These days, he continues to shape surf culture through his writing — producing thoughtful, no-nonsense blogs that chronicle Aotearoa’s surf scene.
After reviewing this year’s New Zealand short films, Craig shared this insight:
“This year’s entries of New Zealand shorties saw a maturing in style and content across the board. It was super exciting to see previous years’ entrants persist and develop their craft, as well as bolts from the blue coming in with heartfelt stories. It’s going to be a great program to tour.”

caption:
Jordan Brando → Digi Chats 2026

Captured just after his packed set on the Traxxside stage.

A conversation with Jordan Brando reflecting on his roots, Canberra, the community, and the journey that shaped his sound.

🎥🌊 Judge Spotlight — @gavinbisman 
If you’ve been anywhere near the NZ surf scene over the past 15+ years, chances are you’ve crossed paths with Gav. Gav’s fingerprints are all over the local surf community and surf industry in Aotearoa — from judging comps, to board riders events and clubs, to working with and helping start surf brands. Gav is also the Event Coordinator for @surfingnz 🕴🏄‍♂️ Anything to do with our surf community, Gav’s the guy. If he’s not on the mic he’s probably in the water… or shooting the shit over a coffee. Gav helped start the ASFF back in the beginning, what a legend. After reviewing this year’s submissions, here’s what Gav had to say: “The standard really was incredible this year. Made for some beautiful film watching and some tough judging. The audience is going to be spoilt this year for sure!” 🤙🏾
High praise from someone who lives and breathes surfing. This year’s programme is stacked — and we can’t wait to share it with you on tour.

🎥🌊 Judge Spotlight — @christyprior 
As we gear up to kick off the 14th Aotearoa Surf Film Festival next Monday in Raglan, we’re proud to introduce our final judge — Christy Prior 🤙
Christy is a professional snowboarder and passionate surfer based out of St Clair, Dunedin. She represented New Zealand at the 2014 Winter Olympics and made history as the first Kiwi snowboarder to medal at the Winter X Games — putting NZ snowboarding firmly on the global map.
Since retiring from the World Pro Tour in 2019, Christy continues to hit the slopes abroad and chases waves closer to home.
After viewing this year’s ASFF programme with her partner and co judge Simon, here’s what she had to say 👇
“The level of surfing both in NZ and around the world is unreal — people are charging and it’s going to be great to see it on the big screen! It’s also amazing to see how important and healing surfing is to so many people. There’s some epic films in this year’s programme.”
High praise to roll into tour week 🙌
📍 Raglan —  Monday @solscape.nz  The 14th ASFF starts here. See you on the big screen.

Muchas gracias a tod@s por acompañarnos 🫂 

Y no se preocupen que esto no acaba! 

Nos vemos en TINTA 2026 🔥

2026 kicked off with both highs and lows.
All beautifully entwined… along with a solid fever that hit me hard just a day before the countdown 😅

Between that and a series of back-to-back programs, I found myself constantly wondering if I was pushing too far or even if my voice would open enough to sing at all. Somehow, it did.

The result was always worth it.

Nimbin Peace Festival held a beautiful, truly peaceful vibe that quickly turned into a full-power solo. Once people locked into the groove, I threw away the plan and leaned into the spontaneous magic I naturally gravitate toward complete with a whirling dervish moment to help send the energy out 😉

That flowed straight into Starlight Festival, where the energy was similar but the entry was gentler. People had just emerged from a beautiful sound healing, so I began with soft Raga and voice exercises…
and then once the electronic tabla started looping haha nearly everyone was dancing and singing in the Raga Flow.
I will share a video someone took shortly. 
(check out my latest reel)
Truth is though it was exhausting I’m always grateful that I persevered and let it happen.

Next stop is SoundKalpa Retreat at Rocklyn Ashram, followed by shows around Melbourne and Newcastle, before wrapping up January back home in the Byron Shire with a full Raga Retreat (which is nearly full now 🙏).

Feeling grateful to have gotten the sickness out of the way early. And while I didn’t quite anchor into New Year’s in the way I had hoped there’s always time to set intention and start fesh again.

Wishing everyone to ride a smooth, expansive wave into 2026 🌊
With love,
Shivam

The Single Fin Mingle 2026 - Men’s Results

Before the men had even hit the water, a late shift in the draw set the tone. With finals pushed to Sunday, current World Champion and 2025 SFM winner @kaielliceflint was forced to withdraw — graciously gifting his spot to a young Hawaiian talent @kohoohikihamakua who hadn’t planned to compete.

Semi-final one delivered a major moment for the home crowd, with Sumner’s own Jack Tyro getting a win over former World Champion Harrison Roach — both surfers posting high scores to progress into the final. In semi-final two, Gold Coast’s Archy Bemrose was the real bolter of the event, earning his place in the final in his first Mingle appearance alongside Mount Maunganui’s Jordan Griffin — still the only two-time Men’s Mingle champion.

The final was a world-class showcase of traditional longboarding. Archy continued his incredible run, finishing second, ahead of local phenom Jack Tyro in third and Jordan Griffin in fourth. But it was Harrison Roach, in his first competition since claiming his 2022 world title, who reminded everyone why he is one of the best of this generation. With clean, head-high lines rolling through, Harrison opened up his full repertoire - delivering what was quite possibly some of the finest longboarding ever seen in a New Zealand contest. A perfect 10 in the scoreline left the rest of the field chasing combinations.

The Mingle, once again, providing a stage for world-class surfing in its purest form.

caption:
The Gliding Award 🤍

@minnierobberds is heading to @glidingbarnacles in Portugal in September 2026.

For over 10 years, The Mingle has shared a special connection with the Gliding Barnacles Festival in Portugal. They’ve become like family – a brother / sister festival to us. So much of our community flows between these two events, and it’s something we’re incredibly proud of.

This year brought one of the most special surprises yet. Before The Mingle, GB founder @euricogoncalves reached out with an idea – to award one SFM surfer a trip to Gliding Barnacles this September. We spoke about how to choose, and landed on something simple: let the surfers decide.

During the event, our surfers were (unknowingly) asked to vote for the person who best embodied the spirit of The Mingle. The prize wasn’t revealed until this moment at Sunday’s prize giving, when Minnie was announced as the recipient of the Gliding Award – chosen by her peers.

Minnie is a Sumner local – a surfer, musician, and all-round beautiful human. She performed at the Friday night street party, competed on Saturday, and spent the weekend commentating. She truly embodies the spirit of these festivals, and we couldn’t be more stoked to see her take this one out.

Thank you @glidingbarnacles ❤️‍🔥

🎥 @williamahunt

Snippit from an interview with @ninenbn newswhile facilitating at @starlightfestival_byron earlier in the year.

We spoke about the power of breathwork and why more and more people are turning to these practices for emotional regulation, stress relief and deeper connection with themselves.

Breathwork is rapidly becoming recognised as a powerful tool for:

- Stress and anxiety regulation
- Emotional release and processing
- Nervous system reset
- Greater clarity and presence
- Deeper mind–body connection
- Safe way to access altered states of consciousness 
- Reducing pain and so much more!

The breath is one of the few systems in the body that is both automatic and consciously controllable, making it a powerful gateway to influencing your physiology, emotions and state of mind.

Simple practices can create profound shifts.

This is why I’m so passionate about sharing this work with leaders, coaches, facilitators and everyday humans who want to live with more presence, power, fulfilment and alignment.

Not every breathwork journey is intense or results in big shifts or releases, but I do find Conscious Connected Breathing with large groups of people definitely gets the energy moving!

Breath is life.

And when you learn to work with it consciously… everything changes.

Let's Get It.

🦁 Scotty

The Mingle Masters 2026 - Official Results

Sunday mornings at The Mingle have traditionally eased in slowly… not this year.

With a growing crew of invitees now in the 50+ bracket and still surfing at an incredibly high level — it felt like the right time to create space for it. The result: our inaugural Mingle Masters Division.

A 16-surfer, mixed field featuring some of the finest traditional loggers from New Zealand, Australia and Japan. A small, invited group but world-class in every sense.

Then we raised the stakes.
Winner takes all. $1,000 cash.
Quite possibly the biggest prize purse we’ve seen for a masters longboard event — and the surfing more than lived up to it.

These are surfers who’ve spent decades shaping their craft, influencing their communities, and guiding the next generation. To see the level still this high and the style still this sharp was something special.

In the end, it was @daryn.mcbride.creative who took it out, showing exactly why he remains one of Australasia’s finest loggers - as well as a respected shaper, artist and creative with plenty more to give.

Huge congratulations to all involved in our first Mingle Masters. This one’s just getting started… watch this space in 2027.

Join Us at the Starlight Festival this Thursday - Sunday ✨ Experience connection, healing, and embodied wisdom at the Starlight Festival. Meet some of our facilitators:
🌿 Jaclyn Cunningham
Jaclyn is a devoted practitioner of Ancestral Lineage Healing, trained through the lineage of Dr Daniel Foor. She is deeply passionate about restoring relationship—with our ancestors, with the land, with the other-than-human beings, and with the greater forces that quietly support our lives.
Through her work, Jaclyn invites participants to reconnect with their ancestral roots, honour what has come before, and access profound support, belonging, and healing that flows through lineage and land. Her offerings create a grounded, reverent space to remember where we come from and how deeply connected we truly are.
🌊 Paige Celestial Secrets
Let’s support the waters of our emotional, mental, and physical bodies through a beautiful, flowing yoga experience. Paige offers a nourishing, open-level class that weaves together yoga asana, pranayama breathwork, and meditation—inviting us to move beyond the surface and drop into the heart.
Paige has taught yoga around the world, studying the roots of the practice in India. Her teaching style is dynamic, compassionate, and deeply inclusive. This session is open to everyone—whether you’re new to yoga or an experienced practitioner. Yoga is for all, and we are forever students, always growing and discovering new perspectives.

The Single Fin Mingle 2026 - Women’s Results

The 12th edition of The Mingle welcomed our biggest women’s field to date, with 48 of the world’s finest longboarders coming together in Sumner.

Saturday served up testing conditions, but as always, the ocean gave back on Sunday - glassy 1–2m lines rolling through for finals day, right when it mattered most.

The international depth of this year’s field was undeniable, with just one Kiwi, Tessa Randrup, pushing through to the semi-finals.

A beautifully close final - just 2 points separating 1st through 4th, and only 0.4 between the top two - a true reflection of the level and style on display.

Kia ora to all the wāhine who brought their wonderful surfing to the water this year. This is what The Mingle is all about.

caption:
Day 2. Highlights

The morning skies cleared as competitors and spectators packed the seawall and foreshore of the esplanade. The Mingle markets were humming, layers of clothing were shed, and Sumner delivered a stunner of a day 🌞 

As the tide pushed in, so did the scores, with some of the world’s best longboarders battling it out to the shore. Just as the last heats were winding up for the day, the sound check for The Street Party could be heard in the distance a couple of blocks away —The Babe Rainbow, Romi Wrights, Great Gable, and The Yurt Party—it’s a big one!

La Huaca de Huantille. 

La cultura Ychsma fue una importante sociedad costeña asentada en los valles de Lurín y Rímac. La cerámica típica es de pasta gruesa, color rojo claro (debido al uso de achiote) y decorada con motivos antropomorfos y zoomorfos, frecuentemente con la técnica de "cara gollete".
Entre sus constantes representaciones de la fauna está el pelícano como símbolo de poder y de lo sagrado, asociado a la élite y los espacios ceremoniales, una muestra de cómo esta cultura plasmó en su arte la profunda relación entre su territorio, sus creencias y su estructura social.

Tuvimos la maravillosa oportunidad de hablar con la arqueóloga de la Huaca de Huantille, aprender sobre esta cultura y sus rituales. Así mismo compartir un espacio de creación con @fateone96 y @sywek.fuego para lograr este bello resultado.

Muchas gracias al @greengraff.art por la invitación a estos espacios 🙌

This is an exploration into masculine–feminine polarity, leadership, safety, and connection, and how these forces shape our relationships, our nervous systems, and our sense of purpose.

We’ll go deeper into what’s been happening to masculinity in the modern world and how initiation has been lost, how our physiology is still that of tribal, hunter-gatherer humans, and why movement, purpose, responsibility, and brotherhood are not optional, but essential. I’ll also be sharing practical insights and live demonstrations around masculine–feminine communication: what sparks polarity, what collapses it, and how to keep it alive in real relationships and everyday life.

Tattooing as a meeting point, but also as a gateway into a much broader universe. This is one of the characteristics that make Barcelona’s @baumfest different from a simple tattoo convention. Organised by Mik Garreta and Laura Cubero, the festival brings together the world of tattooing with the many expressions of urban culture: from large murals to sculpture, as well as dance, BMX, customised cars and the Muay Thai ring.

This edition, however, took place during an especially challenging weekend for Barcelona. The weather emergency caused serious mobility problems across the city, making it difficult to get around and inevitably affecting attendance at the event. On Saturday night, moreover, due to the measures communicated by Barcelona City Council in response to the emergency situation, the convention had to close earlier than scheduled. A significant interruption that altered the programme for the day, but did not prevent the artists from continuing to work or the festival from maintaining its character.

Discover more on www.tattoolife.com 🔗 https://www.tattoolife.com/baum-tattoo-fest-tattooing-and-urban-culture-in-the-heart-of-barcelona/

En esta producción completamente femenina, la escaladora canadiense de 32 años @bronwynhodgins tras años en expediciones en grandes paredes decide cambiar su enfoque hacia la escalada deportiva.

Lo que no sabe es que esta nueva curiosidad por el entrenamiento y el rendimiento la llevará a la experiencia mental más intensa de su vida… mientras se entrega por completo en encadenar La Rubia, en Villanueva del Rosario (Andalucía).

Mira la película patrocinada por @rab.equipment / @rab_noticias el viernes 14 de noviembre en el Teatre La Renaixença (Cornudella de Montsant). 

Entrada gratuita, no se requiere reserva.

[ENG]

In this all-female production, 32-year-old Canadian climber @bronwynhodgins faces a burnout from Big Wall expeditions and decides to shift her focus to sport climbing. 

Little does she know that this new curiosity for training and performance will plunge her into the most intense mental undertaking of her life… as she pours herself into La Rubia, a 5.14c (8c+) in Villanueva del Rosario, Spain.

Watch the film on Friday, 14 November at Teatre La Renaixença (Cornudella de Montsant). Free admission, no reservation required.

@ykartbookfair 2026 resmi berakhir. Tapi mungkin, yang paling tertinggal bukan hanya karya-karya yang dipamerkan, melainkan percakapan, pertemuan, dan rasa terhubung yang muncul di dalamnya.

Selama tiga hari, Yogyakarta Art Book Fair mempertemukan pekerja kreatif, seniman, penerbit independen, hingga komunitas lintas negara dalam satu ruang yang dipenuhi artbook, zine, workshop, diskusi, dan pertukaran ide. Di tengah industri kreatif yang semakin cepat dan individual, ruang seperti ini terasa semakin penting karena kreativitas tidak hanya tumbuh dari kemampuan untuk terus terlihat, tetapi juga dari kemampuan untuk saling terhubung.

Melalui praktik penerbitan independen, YKABF menunjukkan bahwa karya tidak selalu hadir sebagai produk akhir semata. Ia juga bisa menjadi medium sosial: membuka percakapan, mempertemukan pengalaman, dan membangun solidaritas lintas komunitas maupun lintas negara.

Dan mungkin, itu yang membuat ruang seperti YKABF terus dibutuhkan oleh kita. 

Terima kasih untuk @ykartbookfair dan semua pihak yang sudah merawat ruang ini bersama-sama. ✨

caption:
Dalam program Special Showcase, YKABF 2026 menghandirkan Ika Vantiani beserta jurnal-jurnal miliknya. Dipajang berderet, serta dipersilakan untuk bisa membolak-balik untuk melihat setiap halamannya. Pameran Junk-to-Journals: Between Undoing and Rewriting Ephemera berangkat dari praktik junk journaling yang dijalankan Ika Vantiani selama beberapa tahun terakhir. Praktik Junk Journal milik Ika Vantiani membawa kita pada kerja menelusuri hubungan antara menemukan, menyusun, dan menata apa yang kita pikirkan. Nasib suatu benda atau objek, agaknya dapat dihentikan, diputus ditengah oleh praktik Junk Journal. Lalu sang pembuat, seperti memberikan nasib yang lebih layak dan bernilai. 

Ada beberapa bagian yang memang tidak diperkenankan untuk didokumentasikan. Yaitu adalah catatan-catatan personal milik Ika Vantiani. Tentu ini perihal menghargai momen dan sekitarnya. Sama seperti bagaimana seluruh jurnal ini dibuat. Walau kita bisa pandang sangat serius, sebagai bentuk pengarsipan, namun kerja seperti ini kami rasa didominasi pada yang lebih manusiawi. Dimana kita punya ruang untuk menghargai secara penuh yang tak terduga, bahkan membaca ulang jurnal yang sudah kita buat pun adalah berkah yang tak terduga. 

Menurut kami, unsur paling menyenangkan dalam kerja-kerja Junk Journal adalah ketidakpastian dan kebaruan yang terus menerus ada. Sekian penelurusan, sekian temuan, juga sekian halaman akan membawa kita kesinambungan yang agaknya absurd. Mungkin tak banyak maksud untuk menyatukan suatu hal, namun akhirnya, kita punya suatu sensasi didalamnya. Coba saja amati bagaimana kombinasi gambar, bentuk, dan material dalam banyak jurnal Ika Vantiani. Memamerkan deretan jurnal ini, adalah langkah yang mengesankan. Agenda ini membuka refleksi kami pada material disekitar, perihal bagaimana budaya konsumsi kita, atau cara kita memperlakukan mereka. Kemungkinan menjadi pusat utama dalam praktik ini, yaitu digunakan kembali, baik secara fungsi maupun narasi. Praktik mengarsipkan pengalaman sehari hari melalui material bekas menunjukkan bahwa ingatan, keterikatan emosional, dan pengalaman hidup dapat hadir melalui medium sederhana. Com uma costa virada a sul e outra a oeste, Sagres tem quase sempre um sítio onde a onda entra. Mas aqui o mar não se domina: respeita-se. O vento muda, a maré sobe, o Atlântico decide. Quem vive em Sagres aprende isso cedo.
O Sagres Sessions nasce desta mistura. Não é só um campeonato nem só um festival. É um encontro entre quem vive do mar e quem vive para ele. Surf, arte, música e mercado, lado a lado, numa vila que abre as portas durante três dias.

As you plan for the year ahead, we want to share an update about On This Rock. The event has been moved from Fall 2026 to Spring 2027 for two reasons: 
🧗‍♂️🧗‍♂️🧗‍♀️
1) Supporting the local climbing community: The first weekend of October this year is going to be the inaugural Smith Rock Climbing Festival, a grassroots event led by our local climb shop, RedPoint (check them out!) 
🧗‍♂️🧗‍♂️🧗‍♀️
Common Ground is excited to support this festival in several ways, and moving OTR allows both events to thrive without overlap. If you love climbing and the PNW climbing community, mark your calendars on October 2-4, 2026 for this first-ever festival!
🧗‍♂️🧗‍♂️🧗‍♀️
2) Fine-tuning On This Rock: Our planning team is using this extra time to assess OTR and dial it in even more toward it’s mission—improving accessibility, experiencing belonging, and considering Jesus in the climbing space. Please keep our team in prayer, reach out to us with any ideas you have for OTR’s future, and block out May 21–23, 2027 for the next OTR!

O Arquipélago - Centro de Artes Contemporâneas e o festival Tremor  desenvolvem, desde 2021, acções regulares de formação, direcionadas a profissionais e curiosos das áreas artísticas. O objetivo do Ciclo é a capacitação de novos agentes culturais locais, dando continuidade ao trabalho que ambas as entidades têm desenvolvido na abertura de novas oportunidades de empoderamento para o território.

A edição 2026/27 do Ciclo pretende criar contexto para a celebração da cultura Rave nos Açores, proporcionando a criação de um coletivo que crie e implemente uma nova festa, que tomará forma durante o presente ano, sendo apresentada durante o Tremor 2027.

Relembramos o que vivemos há um mês, quando abrimos as portas a uma edição que se fez residência de novas e bonitas memórias. 

De concertos no fundo da piscina até às alturas de um miradouro; 
A nossa nova casa, as casas que se abriram para momentos gastronómicos e as muitas casas em cartazes espalhados pela ilha;
A cartografia imaginária, sensorial e sonora de São Miguel, criada a muitas mãos no Ciclo.
 
A resposta é dançar, o palco é o playground, e o #tremoréamor. 

O Tremor regressa à ilha de São Miguel, nos Açores, entre os dias 16 e 20 de março de 2027.
A última fase de Passes Gerais está aberta. Compra o teu em tremor-pdl.com.

Throwback to what we experienced a month ago, when we opened the doors to an edition that became home to new and beautiful memories.

Concerts from the bottom of a pool to the heights of a viewpoint; 
Our new home, the houses that opened their doors for gastronomic experiences, and the many houses on posters scattered around the island;
The imaginary, sensory, and sonic cartography of São Miguel, created by many hands in Ciclo.

The answer is to dance, the stage is the playground, and #tremoréamor.

ACT Natimuk/Nati Frinj Biennale has a long history within the township of Natimuk and the surrounding areas, and we are devastated, along with the entire community, by the impacts of the bushfire on Friday 9 January. While we are deeply thankful that no human lives were lost, many lives have been changed forever through the loss of homes, property, and the deep connections that come with them.

Although it is still very early days, Natimuk, as the resilient community it is, has already moved into support mode, caring for those most directly impacted. Our heartfelt thoughts are with everyone who is still reeling from these losses, and we hope that in the near future we can offer support and space in the ways we know best.

We cannot thank emergency services enough, both during the fire itself and throughout the ongoing aftermath. Firefighters, along with community members who stayed to defend properties, are the reason much of the township still stands. Essential services—including power, water and communications—were largely reinstated by Sunday evening, no small feat given the number of power poles destroyed. And community members who have stepped up to guide people towards support options ad offer help.

Thank you to all who have reached out with messages of care and understanding—both personally and as fellow arts organisations and supporters. Kind words at a time like this truly matter - there is a long road ahead for the community.

𝗘𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘁: booound: Yogyakarta Art Book Fair 2026

Yogyakarta Art Book Fair (YKABF) (@ykartbookfair) will take place from 8 to 10 May at Langgeng Art Space. This third edition continues the fair’s celebration of the independent publishing scene in Indonesia and beyond. It explores the intersection of physical materiality and conceptual innovation in contemporary publishing practices. 

“The theme of YKABF 2026, "booound," originates from the term binding in the publishing production process. Binding is the process of uniting loose pages into a publication. We use this technical term simultaneously as a conceptual proposal to discuss the things that bind us, whether as a community or other more fluid forms of togetherness.”

The YKABF team shares more about the foundations of the fair, this year’s theme booound and the resonance of the event for the art publishing community in Indonesia and beyond.

Com direção artística de Raquel Castro, Ínsula assume-se como um território de experimentação e encontro, onde fronteiras entre interior e exterior se diluem, abrindo espaço a novas formas de perceção e relação.

On an Azorean island 1,500km away from mainland Portugal, there’s a quaint music and arts festival that puts its unique location at centre stage.

What an incredible experience was Journey of the Karen. Created by members of the Karen communities in Horsham and Nhill, in collaboration with Black Hole Theatre, this immersive multi-media production brought together traditional storytelling and contemporary performance in the most powerful way.

Told by performers across generations and cultures – with giant glowing puppets, original music, and evocative video – the work spoke not only to the Karen experience, but to the journeys of so many migrants: stories of persecution, resistance, escape, and survival. It was a moving testament to community strength and the importance of sharing stories that too often go untold.

All script, sets, video, music, props, and puppets were created by community members under the guidance of Black Hole Theatre’s brilliant creative team.  Images: Suzanne Phoenix

ACT Natimuk in partnership with Gariwerd Wimmera Reconciliation Network and Regional Arts Victoria (VicHealth grant) are proud to present a Reconciliation Week 2026 event. The theme this is year is 'All in On Reconciliation' and our event 'Storytelling through Film' is an evening of conversation and connection. It connects a lot of what ACT Natimuk does in the space of arts, combining storytelling, film and circus alongside its support for First Peoples, providing a welcoming and safe space for all community to come and learn, reflect and enjoy powerful storytelling through film.

The event features a screening and conversation with Dylan Singh around The Story of Becoming Nala, a short film based on Alan Murphy and Chrissie Secombes book Becoming Nala, exploring Alan's journey of reconnecting with Country, culture, and identity.

#nationalreconciliationweek2026 #allinforreconciliation #becomingnala #actnatimuk #natimuk #horshamvictoria 

Alan and Chrissie were recipients of ACT Natimuk’s inaugural First Nations Creative Lab grant in 2023/24, and Dylan is the 2024/25 recipient. This work continues to develop through a project that ACT Natimuk are delivering in partnership with Regional Arts Victoria as part of VicHealth’s 'Shifting the Playbook initiative'.

The evening also includes 'The Colleano Heart', a powerful documentary examining Aboriginal identity through the story of Australia’s famous Colleano circus family. This connects beautifully with Dylan’s background as a second-generation circus performer and ACT Natimuk's own programming with its monthly Circus Jam sessions.

Please join us – the event is free, no booking required, and we will have refreshments during a short intermission break.

Like a side of stories with your food?

The Sky Could Be Blue
Black Hole Theatre

Delicious food, secret stories—are you eavesdropping or in the show? Sky Could Be Blue is an immersive, multi-sensory experience that transports audiences into the world of the Vietnamese and southeast asian diaspora in Australia. Audience and cast, all wearing headphones, mingle as patrons, waiters and passersby. Dining out becomes an experience of permitted eavesdropping… 

You’ll hear stories of dating struggles, generational tensions, hidden political divides, and the hopes and fears of those navigating life between cultures. Never a lecture, they are tender and abstract, emotional, funny, deeply personal. As audience you can choose to interact or simply enjoy the food!

Make your reservation now. Tickets here - https://natifrinj.com/sky-could-be-blue/

OFFICIAL STATEMENT – Brisbane Street Art Festival 2026

After more than a decade of transforming Brisbane’s walls and public spaces into living art, we have some deeply disappointing news to share.

BSAF will not be taking place in 2026. This was not a decision we came to lightly. Over many months, our small and dedicated team explored every available avenue to secure the funding needed to present a festival worthy of this city. Despite that sustained effort, we were unable to proceed.

A free, large-scale public art festival of BSAF’s scope depends on meaningful investment from government and partners. That investment did not come together for 2026. We are continuing to engage with all levels of government and the arts sector to make the case for renewed support.

A Decade That Changed This City
Since 2016, BSAF has supported hundreds of artists to deliver more than 400 works of public art across Brisbane — from Northshore to Spring Hill, the Airport to the CBD. We’ve brought world-class artists to our streets: Rachael Sarra, Fintan Magee, Sofles, Guido van Helten, Adnate, Said Dokins, Sor Two, and many more. BSAF has not just displayed art. It has created artists, built careers, sparked conversations, and made the case that public space belongs to everyone.

Building The Path To 2027
This is a pause, not a full stop. We are forming a 2027 steering group, bringing together artists, cultural leaders, and community advocates, to build the foundations for BSAF’s return. We’ll be sharing updates on that work and our advocacy for the sustained public arts investment this city deserves.

If you believe in what BSAF represents, we need your voice now. Write to your local councillor. Share this statement. Tag us and tell your story. Every message sent is a vote for the kind of city Brisbane chooses to be.

To our artists, volunteers, partners, and audiences, you didn’t just attend this festival. You made it. 

The walls are still out there. The art is still standing. And so are we.

With love, gratitude and determination,
Lincoln Savage & Joelle Wong
Brisbane Street Art Festival

I had the privilege of travelling to Brisbane, Australia to take part in @bsafest, and is one of the most significant experiences of my artistic practice.
Australia gave me encounters with artists, communities and people of extraordinary generosity and talent, amazing people like @aletheabeetson , @shanifinch , @burgkaba , @jadescott_ , @thatlincoln , @qt_, @mitchsmegapixels, @lukesmitheram, @gothdayout, @simplebao, @grisone, @toksojophoto, @carlia_louise, @vanessasuzette_makeup , @nube_jaguar, @mstdesign, @itsamye, @emohbrien , @kittyonthemountain and so many others with whom I shared walls, conversations and that particular energy that only happens when so many creative people come together.
There I painted two murals under the concept Sleeping Languages in Queensland: a tribute to the Aboriginal cultures and languages of Queensland. It was deep work, built from listening to organisations like @digiyoutharts and shaped by the words that the people of Brisbane shared with me.
I remember that after months of paperwork like visas, permits, forms, I turned up to my first meeting with Digi Youth Arts with a boring slide presentation, very institutional, very formal. And Digi Youth simply introduced themselves with a beautiful song that gave me goosebumps. That moment reminded me that community, art and connection always come first, everything else is just admin.
Today BSAF shares some difficult news: the festival will not be going ahead in 2026 due to a lack of government funding. A festival that over a decade produced more than 400 murals and transformed the public identity of an entire city deserves every bit of support it can get.
The walls are still standing, the art is still there, and so are we. Public art is not a luxury, it’s a community right. 🙏🏽 @brisbanecitycouncil @artsqueensland help #BSAFEST

Welcome to Natimuk and the Nati Frinj Biennale 2025

Nestled on the traditional lands of the Wotjobaluk Peoples in the West Wimmera, Natimuk is a small town with a big creative heart — where art, community, and landscape are deeply entwined. Halfway between Melbourne and Adelaide, and watched over by Dyurrite (Mount Arapiles) with Gariwerd (the Grampians) nearby, it’s a place of natural wonder and cultural vitality.

During the Nati Frinj Biennale, this quiet town bursts to life — streets, paddocks and halls transform into stages, galleries and playgrounds for artists, locals and visitors alike.

Experience the Frinj:
• Site-specific works transforming Natimuk’s spaces
• Live performances across theatre, dance, music and circus
• Interactive installations, workshops and unexpected encounters
• A weekend celebrating art, adventure and community under the wide Wimmera sky

Come for the festival — stay for the place. Explore Dyurrite’s climbs, Gariwerd’s trails, and the vast beauty of the Wimmera plains. Discover why Natimuk’s creative spirit draws artists, adventurers and dreamers from near and far.

Many thanks to our major festival sponsor Visit Victoria @visitmelbourne

Journey of the Karen is a ground-breaking new performance created by Karen communities in Horsham and Nhill with Black Hole Theatre.

From Myanmar’s mountain villages, through refugee camps in Thailand, to new lives in western Victoria—this immersive, multi-media production shares powerful stories of survival and resilience.
Told through giant glowing puppets, music, video, and traditional storytelling, it’s a moving testament to the strength of community and the importance of untold stories.

Creative Team: Nancy Black, Alistair Shaw, Christinedah Gaw, Hser Wah Po John Bolton, Dave Jones, Mary French, David Franzke, Tracey Skinner, Abstract Projects

“Becoming Nala” is a digital short film led by First Nations artists on Wotjobaluk Country in northwest Victoria. Inspired by Alan Murphy’s personal journey to reconnect with Country and discover his father’s birthplace, the project celebrates survival and resilience.

In collaboration with Dylan Singh from The Dreaming project, it brings together mob to share stories through art of film, animation, and ceremony, honouring First Nations storytelling traditions and the strength of community, culture, and connection.

You're invited to sit and listen to the story of Becoming Nala.

Artists: Alan Murphy, Christina Secombe & Mat Dooling in collaboration with Creative Producer Dylan Singh (The Dreaming Project) & Lee Ramseyer bache and Ivan Masic (Little projector Company)

Calling Country: The Land Speaks Back, presented on Melbourne’s Hamer Hall Facade, explores the power of dance as a language that speaks with the land and our more-than-human kin. Through somatic ecologies and kinships, dance connects First Peoples to land, topographies, and sky stories. The series brings together local and international First Peoples artists, sharing transnational connections and reflecting on reciprocal relationships with the land. It launched with films by the Djirri Djirri Wurundjeri Women’s Dance Group and internationally recognized artist Cannupa Hanska Luger.

Presented throughout the heart of Naarm/Melbourne, RISING is a festival of new art, music, and performance. Luger’s Midéegaadi also welcomed festival artists and audiences into a shared space for reflection, connection, and reciprocity.

COMUNICADO OFICIAL
Con profundo pesar informamos que la Convención de Tatuajes La Plata queda
suspendida. Esta decisión responde a factores externos y ajenos a nuestra organización.
El municipio desde la intendencia modificó la fecha del evento en más de tres
oportunidades y, posteriormente, intentó adelantarla casi un mes. Finalmente, resolvió de
manera unilateral cancelar todos los eventos privados previstos tanto para este año como
para el próximo.
Hasta último momento trabajamos activamente en la búsqueda de una solución que permitiera sostener esta edición, pero, lamentablemente, no fue posible.
Detrás de cada edición hay meses de trabajo, organización, coordinación con artistas y
proveedores, reservas confirmadas y una importante inversión económica y personal. Nos
duele profundamente no poder concretar, una vez más, una convención del nivel que
nuestro público merece.
Nos pondremos en contacto de manera personal con cada artista y expositor para
coordinar la devolución de las señas correspondientes.
Queremos pedir disculpas sinceras. 
Somos conscientes del esfuerzo que también implicó de parte de ustedes, y comprendemos plenamente la frustración que esta noticia genera.
Esta situación nos afecta especialmente porque esta iba a ser nuestra 15.ª edición: una despedida significativa de una etapa, pensada para dar paso a un nuevo formato.
Sin embargo, no nos rendimos. Ya estamos trabajando en la búsqueda de una nueva
sede para volver a encontrarnos.
Esta situación fue provocada por terceros y resulta completamente ajena a nuestra
voluntad. De nuestra parte, agotamos todas las instancias posibles hasta el último
momento.
Agradecemos profundamente el acompañamiento, la confianza y la participación
sostenida durante tantos años. Porque, si algo aprendimos en todo este tiempo, es que
ustedes fueron, son y seguirán siendo la convención.
Esto no termina acá. Nos volveremos a encontrar con nuevo formato y nueva  locación.

The sixth and final 2026 First Peoples Melbourne Art Tram has launched: Mitch Mahoney’s (Boonwurrung and Barkindji) ‘Pale Blue’. Mitch’s tram is an A Class 236, riding on route 12.

“The Mulloway and the Tuna are two of the largest and most powerful fish to visit Naarm’s waters. These species carry old stories of the movements of Sea Country. Pale Blue brings the celestial and the marine together, imagining a space where sky and sea meet — where Ancestral memory, ecological knowledge and Blak imagination flow into one another. The fish become not just animals, but living archives, carrying stories for the next generation.” — Mitch Mahoney

Born in North-West Victoria along the banks of the Murray River, Mitch Mahoney is a Boonwurrung/Barkindji artist who grew up in Mildura and the Hunter Valley. He currently splits his time between Melbourne and regional NSW.

As a multidisciplinary artist, Mitch focuses on the revitalisation of southeastern Aboriginal practices, creating cultural items such as possum skin cloaks, traditional stringy bark and red gum canoes, and kangaroo tooth necklaces. He also specialises in line drawings and southeastern Aboriginal design. His art reflects his Country and the natural connection he feels to all that it supports, creates and provides, and the ever-changing influence it has on him.

The fifth 2026 First Peoples Melbourne Art Tram has launched: Jenna Mayilema Lee’s (Larrakia, Wardaman, KarraJarri) ‘burn before reading’. Jenna’s tram is a C1 Class 3023, riding on routes 48 and 109.

“After fire, eucalypts produce vivid green growth against their charred, blackened trunks. In ‘burn before reading’ each leaf is cut from the pages of ‘Aboriginal Words and Place Names’ by A.W. Reed, a flawed, still-in-print colonial text that undermines the richness of First Nations languages. By reconstructing these pages, the tram becomes a living eco-system of words, imagining language as both archive and future, asserting that First Languages, like Country itself, endure beyond trauma.” — Jenna Mayilema Lee

Jenna Mayilema Lee is a Gulumerridjin (Larrakia), Wardaman, and KarraJarri woman with Japanese, Chinese, Filipino, Irish and Scottish ancestry. Her practice explores language, materiality, and the transformation of inherited narratives. Fascinated by what is lost in translation, she investigates the spaces between words, capturing the subtleties of language through immersive installations, works on paper, sculpture, and multimedia. 

Working primarily with books as colonial artefacts, Jenna interrogates dictionaries that poorly document First Peoples’ languages, combining these sources with Larrakia linguistics to reflect on the world she observes. Through deconstruction and reconstruction, she engages with materials that echo the past, revealing hidden stories and the unseen forces shaping our understanding of history and identity.

Presented in partnership with Transport Victoria and Yarra Trams

The fourth 2026 First Peoples Melbourne Art Tram has launched: Sonja Hodge’s (Lardil) ‘spirits, yaka & jirndi’. Sonja’s tram is a D2 Class 5002, riding on routes 6 and 19.

“This work reflects my connections to family, belonging to Country, loss, and how I feel and see myself in this world. It is a celebration and a homage to all the strong women and men who came before me and the path made easier for me by them. I dedicate my work to my children and mob; I want to show them what is stirring inside me and what I carry with me always.” — Sonja Hodge

Sonja Hodge is a Lardil artist born in 1969 in Meekatharra on Wajarri Yamatji land, Western Australia. She moved to Melbourne in 1990, where she worked and studied before settling in Mildura in 1996 and has recently returned to Melbourne. Sonja has over 30 years of experience in the arts, spanning printmaking, painting, photography, silversmithing, and multimedia. Her work explores her deep connections to culture, family, community, and the world around her.

Sonja has contributed to numerous public art projects and exhibitions, including the landmark state-wide exhibition ‘We Iri We Homeborn’ and education project Can’t See For Lookin’ – Koorie Women Artists Educating (1993). Her work has shown with the Melbourne Fringe Festival, Alcaston Gallery, Wartook Studio Gallery, and The Art Vault. In 2021, Sonja had a solo exhibition at Blak Dot Gallery and exhibited in Seen and Unseen at the Koorie Heritage Trust. Last year, she was selected for the Agency x La Trobe Art Institute Residency and exhibited Shadows: Blak, White & Blue at Workspace 3496.

The third 2026 First Peoples Melbourne Art Tram has launched: Zena Zada Cumpston’s (Barkandji/Kurnu) ‘ngamaka/mother (#1,#2,#3)’. Zena’s tram is a D1 Class 3502, riding on routes 5, 6, 16, and 72 for the next 12 months.

“The abundance our mother (Country) offers is ever-present. She watches you carefully as you take. If we fail to be in reciprocity with her, our access to abundance can, and will, be denied. ngamaka/mother speaks to active custodianship, intergenerational learning and the need to practice, hold and re-invigorate all that Ancestors have passed on. ngamaka/mother insists that we have been handed all we need to thrive and to enact healing for people and for Country.” — Zena Zada Cumpston

Zena Zada Cumpston is a Barkandji woman with Afghan, English, and Irish heritage. Zena works as an artist, writer, consultant, and educator. She is passionate about plants and seeks out projects that empower community and Country. She is a member of the Birrarung Council and a widely published writer. Zena was co-author of the 2021 Federal State of the Environment Report and the book ‘Plants; past, present, future’. She regularly works as a public speaker.
Zena has participated in various local and international artist residencies, exhibitions and gatherings centred around land-based practices and First Nations knowledges in artmaking. She is the 2026 recipient of the Bandalang Artist Residency at the Australian National University. In 2026, her art will be featured across several projects, including the ‘Watch These Hands’ exhibition (Heide Museum of Modern Art) and as an artist in residence at the Irish Museum of Modern Art (IMMA) in Dublin.
